questions.answer: An ammeter measures electric current. A voltmeter measures potential difference.
accepted_alternatives: Ammeter: current; voltmeter: voltage or potential difference.
questions.tolerance: Both quantities must be matched to the correct meter.

marking_points.text: States that an ammeter measures electric current
States that a voltmeter measures potential difference

questions.answer: A, a diagonal arrow across the resistor

option_feedback.A: Correct: the diagonal arrow marks an adjustable resistance.
option_feedback.B: A surrounding circle is not the distinguishing feature of a variable resistor.
option_feedback.C: One long and one short line form a cell symbol.
option_feedback.D: A voltmeter is shown by V inside a circle, not inside a resistor.

marking_points.text: Selects A, identifying the diagonal arrow as the distinguishing feature of a variable resistor

option_feedback.A: An unconnected cell terminal leaves a gap.
option_feedback.B: A crossing without a junction dot does not by itself complete the intended path.
option_feedback.C: Correct: the continuous returning path is a complete loop through all three components.
option_feedback.D: Distance on the page does not determine electrical connection.

marking_points.text: Selects C, identifying a continuous returning path as the complete circuit

option_feedback.A: A voltmeter in the main path is not connected across the lamp.
option_feedback.B: Correct: the two voltmeter leads join the two lamp terminals.
option_feedback.C: This measures across the ammeter, not across the lamp.
option_feedback.D: Both voltmeter leads need defined connection points.

marking_points.text: Selects B, placing the voltmeter across the two terminals of the lamp

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: X is an open switch. Y is a lamp.
accepted_alternatives: X: open switch; Y: bulb or filament lamp.
parts.tolerance: Each component must be identified from its symbol.

marking_points.text: Identifies X as an open switch
Identifies Y as a lamp

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Remove the voltmeter from the main loop and reconnect it on a separate branch whose two ends join the two terminals of lamp Y.
accepted_alternatives: Connect the voltmeter in parallel across Y, with one lead at each end of Y.
parts.tolerance: The answer must specify both removal from the main path and connection across Y.

marking_points.text: Removes the voltmeter from its series position in the main loop
Reconnects the voltmeter across the two terminals of lamp Y

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A complete circuit using correct cell, closed-switch, ammeter, LDR, lamp and voltmeter symbols. The cell, switch and ammeter lie in the supply path; the LDR and lamp occupy separate branches between the same two junctions; the voltmeter is connected across the LDR only.
accepted_alternatives: Any layout preserving the stated connectivity and prescribed symbols.
parts.tolerance: Component order in the unbranched supply path and overall page layout may vary.

marking_points.text: Uses the prescribed symbols for the cell, closed switch, ammeter, LDR, lamp and voltmeter
Draws a complete supply path containing the cell, closed switch and ammeter
Connects the LDR and lamp on separate branches between the same two junctions
Connects the voltmeter across the two terminals of the LDR only

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The ammeter measures current, so it is placed in the path carrying the current to the branches. The voltmeter measures potential difference, so its two leads connect across the two terminals of the LDR.
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent explanation matching current to the in-path ammeter and potential difference to the across-component voltmeter.
parts.tolerance: Both meter placements must be justified by the quantity measured.

marking_points.text: Explains that the ammeter measures current and is therefore placed in the measured current path
Explains that the voltmeter measures potential difference and is therefore connected across the two LDR terminals
